appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Charlus ne me trompa... que parce qu'il s'y trompait lui-même... il ne faisait rien, n'écrivait pas, ne peignait pas, ne lisait même rien d'une manière sérieuse et approfondie; supérieur aux gens du monde de plusieurs degrés..., il n'était pas pour cela compris par eux; il pouvait tout au plus dégager le charme fallacieux des gens du monde [comme le renne pour les Esquimaux].
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator credits Charlus with a real superiority over society people but immediately qualifies it: his own fascination with the world was self-deception born of unproductiveness, he goes unrecognized by the very people he studies, and his gift is reduced to pre-digesting an illusory charm for others (the reindeer simile), so the net movement leans toward diminishment despite the acknowledged gift.

appraisal_events.evidence: la princesse de Guermantes était placée par M. de Charlus sur le trône le plus élevé... l'adoration excitée principalement par certaines femmes.
appraisal_events.explanation: Among the women Charlus reveres, the princesse de Guermantes is singled out as occupying his highest throne of admiration, elevating her within his private hierarchy, though this is reported as his subjective enthusiasm rather than flatly endorsed by the narrator.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus's claimed penetration into society's true values is undercut by his own self-deception, unproductiveness, and the fact that he goes unrecognized by the people he draws on, so his standing in the passage tilts downward despite the acknowledged superiority.
She is locally elevated as the foremost object of Charlus's fervent admiration among society women, though the elevation is filtered through his subjective enthusiasm.

ambiguities: The closing lines assert that 'there is some objective reality' behind these social distinctions after describing Charlus's view of the princesse de Guermantes as part of 'grossissements artificiels' (artificial magnifications) tied to subjective viewpoints; it is unclear how much of Charlus's exalted placement of her is narrator-endorsed versus reported as his own illusion.
